corrections_to_my_own_earlier_claims: I reported 'clicking does nothing / pointer picking never fires'. WRONG. force-graph signals hover with a `clickable` CSS class, not inline canvas.style.cursor, which is what I was polling - so every 'zero hover hits' measurement measured nothing.

I reported the DPR scale was lost (transform 0.913 vs dpr 1.25). WRONG. 0.9134 / 1.25 = 0.7308 = the d3-zoom factor; the transform includes zoom, so the scale WAS applied. I mis-read my own instrument and called it a confirmed root cause.

Consequence: the two changes I made on that theory (rounding the observed width, remounting via `key`) fixed nothing. The `key` remount was reverted - it would have reset the graph layout on every window resize for no benefit. The rounding was kept as hygiene only, and its comment says so.
real_cause: onNodeClick was always wired and always fired when a click landed on a node. Only 1.2% of the canvas was over a node, with 5px targets, so a person aiming at a dot they can see misses it repeatedly. Fixed with nodePointerAreaPaint: a 10px screen-space pointer target painted independently of the visible dot, divided by globalScale so zooming out does not shrink it back.
